free_tier.stated: no free tier; the 16 GB Windows plan is USD 16.00 a month for 6 CPU cores, 16 GB of RAM and 100 GB of NVMe

retention.stated: the disk persists while the plan is paid; the page states no deletion clock

egress.terms: 8000 GB a month on a 10 Gigabit port, stated on the plan line

interface_detail: Windows is a selectable image at order; the admin path is RDP on the issued IPv4
chaining: a second USD 16 row beside DataWagon, with more transfer and less disk. It replaces neither the Rabisu row nor the Layer7 row on price.
limits_note: the page prints the byte allowance and the port. It prints no licence sentence, so the operating-system cost is unknown.
binding_note: 8 TB is the published ceiling; the licence is the open cost, not a quota.

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at order; the checkout was not completed

reliability_note: no reliability event observed the 16 GB plan was orderable on the page read, while an earlier USD 11 listing was out of stock.
confidence_note: the shape, the single billing cycle and the USD 16.00 price are printed on the order page, and the Linux twin at the same shape is printed at USD 11.00 for one month, so the USD 5.00 Windows layer is arithmetic on two vendor prices and is inferred rather than stated. The licence treatment is absent rather than stated, which is the field that keeps this at documented: no licence wording appears on the package page or the config page.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'Intel KVM VPS 16GB - Windows - Ohio ... 1 Month @ $16.00 ... 6 CPU Cores ... 100 GB NVMe SSD ... 8000 GB Bandwidth'
quoted: 'Intel KVM VPS 16GB - Windows - Texas ... 1 Month @ $16.00 ... 6 CPU Cores ... 100 GB NVMe SSD ... 8000 GB Bandwidth'

the Windows config page carries exactly one cycle, '<option value="130" selected="selected">1 Month @ $16.00</option>', and the only configurable field is a hostname; no licence line and no licence wording appears

the Linux twin at the same 6 cores, 16 GB and 100 GB shape prints two cycles, '1 Month @ $11.00' and '1 Year @ $132.00', so 16.00 minus 11.00 is USD 5.00 and that is the arithmetic value of the Windows layer at this vendor

notes: The page sells the Windows plan by name and prints no licence price. The vendor sells the same machine twice: the Linux twin at the identical 6 core, 16 GB, 100 GB shape is USD 11.00 a month, so the Windows layer is USD 5.00 by implication. That 5.00 is arithmetic on two printed vendor prices, not a printed licence line, and it is the cheapest Windows layer found anywhere in the sweep: it sits beside Virtarix at USD 16.00 and Kimsufi at USD 34.00. The 4 GB plan is USD 4.00 and the 8 GB plan is USD 8.00, so the ladder is USD 1 per GB of RAM and the Windows product line is priced on top of it. A buyer who needs a licence in writing should ask before ordering, because the 5.00 is a price difference and not a statement of what it buys.

extras.windows_layer_basis: arithmetic, 16.00 minus 11.00 on two printed vendor prices at the same shape; not a printed licence line
